holidays.name: Towel Day
holidays.description: Fans of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy carry a towel with them all day. They wear it, drape it over a shoulder, and bring it to work, on the bus, or to the pub. The idea is to be a hoopy frood who always knows where their towel is.
holidays.origin: Towel Day began in 2001, two weeks after author Douglas Adams died on May 11, 2001. Fans created it as a tribute. In his books, a towel is the most useful item a space hitchhiker can own.
holidays.funFact: In the books, a towel can be used as a blanket, a weapon, a signal flag, or a way to shield your eyes from a monster. The belief is that anyone with a towel must also have everything else they need.

holidays.name: Geek Pride Day
holidays.description: This is a day for fans of sci-fi, gaming, comics, coding, and every other nerdy hobby to celebrate their passions without apology. Fans mark it with movie marathons, cosplay, and trivia nights.
holidays.origin: It began in Spain in 2006 as Día del Orgullo Friki. It spread worldwide and is tied to the anniversary of the original Star Wars film, which premiered on May 25, 1977.
holidays.funFact: The date was chosen partly because of Star Wars, and it also falls on Towel Day. Geeks can therefore celebrate two things with one outfit.

holidays.name: Clown Day in Peru
holidays.description: Peru celebrates its clowns with a joyful, colorful parade. Thousands of professional clowns march in full costume, with big shoes, red noses, and a lot of laughter.
holidays.origin: This is a traditional annual observance in Peru that honors the country's professional clowns and the happiness they bring to people. It is held every May 25.
holidays.funFact: The parade draws thousands of professional clowns from all over the country, which makes it one of the biggest gatherings of clowns anywhere.
